title: The Forgotten Contributors: Players Who Shaped Gujarat Titans Beyond Headlines
dek: Franchise histories are told through long-serving stars. The players who passed through Gujarat Titans in a season or two, and still left a mark, are easier to forget.
excerpt: JC Buttler and Mohammed Shami each made a substantial contribution to Gujarat Titans in two seasons or fewer. Short stays like theirs fill in the parts of the history the headlines skip.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Beyond the Headlines
body: Franchise histories are usually told through the players who stayed longest. But every season also depends on short-stay contributors who arrive, perform and move on.
{{ev:fc-n}} players have batted or bowled for Gujarat Titans in two seasons or fewer.

sections.heading: Short Stays, Real Contributions
body: Among them, {{ev:fc-r1}} scored the most runs, {{ev:fc-r1n}}. The chart lists the leading run-scorers among short-stay players.
With the ball, {{ev:fc-w1}} took the most wickets among them, {{ev:fc-w1n}}.

sections.heading: Why They Are Forgotten
body: Short-stay players rarely become the faces of a franchise, whatever they contribute. Public memory follows tenure and captaincy more than output.

sections.heading: Counting, Not Ranking
body: Runs and wickets reward opportunity: a player who batted more scored more. This article lists contributions, not a judgement of who was best.
The salary-versus-contribution model elsewhere in this series weighs contributions against opportunity.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Credit the Passers-Through
body: Gujarat Titans' history includes real contributions from players who stayed only briefly. JC Buttler and Mohammed Shami are the leading examples.
A full history should include them.
